newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli court frees settler charged in boy's death.
newsitem.headline: Israeli court frees settler charged in boy's death.

text.p: An Israeli court freed a Jewish settler on trial for the death of an 11-year-old Palestinian boy, army radio said on Tuesday.
It said the court in Jerusalem agreed on Monday that Nahum Kurman could stay with his wife's family in northern Israel until his trial resumes in about two months.
Kurman, security chief of the Jewish settlement on Hadar Beitar, has been accused of manslaughter in the death last year of Hilmi Shousha, 11, from the West Bank village of Husan.
Israeli authorities say Kurman kicked the boy to the ground, placed his foot on the boy's neck and beat him on the head with a pistol butt while on a hunt for stone throwers.
Kurman faces up to 20 years in jail if convicted.

Palestinian officials said Herzl Getz, chief of Israel's security liaison committee with the Palestinians, had on Sunday met his counterpart Ziad al-Atrash along with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

But they played down an Israel Radio report that the meeting marked a resumption of security cooperation between Israelis and Palestinians halted more than three months ago when Israel broke ground on a new Jewish settlement.

A PLO official who declined to be identified said Arafat made clear during the meeting that the only cooperation with Israel of interest to Palestinians was cooperation that also included the United States, the main broker in peace moves.

The official said Arafat told Getz the Palestinians did not want to escalate violence or confront Israelis but bilateral cooperation would only resume when work was halted on the settlement at the outskirts of Arab East Jerusalem.
The Israeli army declined comment on the radio report.
Israeli military sources said no one was injured on Monday night when an explosive device was thrown at an Israeli bus near the Ofarim Jewish settlement close to Ramallah in the West Bank.
The device exploded, causing light damage to the bus.
